hook_text: In 1872 some black diggers owned claims in the Kimberley Mine. By 1888 black workers were locked in compounds. What happened?
clip_script: Kimberley, 1872. A hill cut into hundreds of little squares, each one a claim. Among the owners are some black and coloured diggers, working their claims and hiring workers. White diggers do not like the competition. They accuse black owners of buying stolen diamonds. In July they riot and burn tents. No law bans black owners by name, but new rules about licences and character certificates do the job. Meanwhile the pit gets deeper. Rock walls collapse. Water floods in. Small diggers sell. Companies form. And from 1885, African workers are locked in compounds for months, searched before they go home. By 1888 one company controls almost everything.
visual_style: A whiteboard grid of claims, some marked with owners' initials that are crossed out one by one, the pit deepening, then a fenced compound drawn beside it.
pacing: Steady at first, tightening as the claims disappear and the fence closes.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and see how a monopoly was built.
